subject: Next steps: procurement route options, marketplace interest, and billing start for trial conversion
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chan <emily.chan@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T13:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: procurement options & trial-to-paid gating — next steps

Hi Emily — great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed path so procurement can pick a route without blocking the pilot: 

- Procurement options we discussed: card (self-serve) vs PO (standard 30-day NET) vs Cloud Marketplace (AWS/Azure) — each has different lead time and invoicing.
- Success criteria for the trial: 3 production test integrations, 500k tokens processed within 30 days, and SLA latency median < 400ms on the test workload.
- Billing start trigger: you asked for flexibility — our recommended approach is to set billing to start on the agreed 'go-live' date (customer-side flag) or automatically 14 days after reaching the usage threshold, whichever comes first.

Attached are two files to help the procurement team: a short procurement checklist (rows: required PO fields, KYC docs, billing contact) and a draft SOW for signature if you need it for internal approval.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Emily / procurement to confirm preferred payment path: PO vs card vs marketplace by Fri 8/7.
2) If PO, send a contact + standard PO template so we can route to finance; we can accept a 30-day NET.
3) If marketplace is preferred, confirm which marketplace and we’ll surface estimated pricing/contract options (adds ~2–3 weeks).
4) Logan & Marissa to prepare final billing start clause for the trial based on your choice.

Happy to jump on a short call with your procurement if that helps — I can include our finance ops lead.

Thanks,
Logan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-sow-draft-v1.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Emily Chan <emily.chan@brightcart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-team@brightcart.com
Date: 2026-08-05T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement options & trial-to-paid gating — next steps

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear recap. A few notes from procurement and product here at BrightCart: 

- Procurement preference: we lean toward PO for our vendor tracking. Card is preferred only for very low-value pilots.
- Marketplace: we are evaluating AWS Marketplace for other vendors, but procurement prefers to keep the PO path if possible because it goes through our internal spend approvals. Marketplace would be a backstop.
- Timing: Procurement can approve a standard PO in ~7–10 business days if the SOW and invoice fields are clearly listed. They specifically need: vendor legal name, remit-to address, tax ID, and a contact for invoice disputes.
- Billing start: product would like the trial to start billing once the trial success criteria are met, not by date. Can you confirm if Redwood can support a billing trigger based on usage threshold (500k tokens) rather than calendar date?

I'll loop in our procure-team alias; they will respond with the PO template and KYC requirements.

Best,
Emily Chan
Product Ops Manager, BrightCart

Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement options & trial-to-paid gating — next steps

Thanks Emily — got it. Short answers below and an ask for the PO template: 

- PO path: yes, Redwood accepts customer POs. We require the PO to list the product line (Redwood Inference Platform), the 30-day NET terms (unless otherwise negotiated), and a billing contact email. Our finance team will return a remittance address + tax ID.
- Billing trigger by usage: yes — we can set billing to begin automatically once the 500k-token threshold is hit (we will record timestamps and provide a usage report). We can also support a customer-side 'go-live' flag if you prefer manual start.
- Marketplace: if you opt for AWS Marketplace we will provide estimated pricing; note that onboarding to marketplace typically adds ~2–3 weeks and fees can change the economics.

ASK: Can procurement send over their PO template and the KYC list (W9/Tax ID or equivalent)? If you send both I will get finance ops to pre-populate and confirm remittance details.

I dropped the two attachments again in case they were missed. Happy to hop on a 20-min call with your procurement this week — propose Fri 8/7 at 10:00am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Logan

Attachments: redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx, redwood-sow-draft-v1.pdf

Logan — quick internal note before the call with BrightCart procurement: 

- I'll own the commercial terms (confirm whether we can accept 30-day NET PO as-is). I will be ready to confirm remittance address and tax ID on the call.
- Vivek — can you be available as backup for any ask about SLA exceptions or expansion pricing? They might press on billing trigger details.
- For the call, we should bring a simple one-slide summary: payment options, timeline impact, and billing-start logic (usage-trigger vs manual go-live).

I will create the one-slide deck and send a link in the calendar invite. If procurement shares the PO template before the call, we can pre-fill and accelerate approval.
